summary: ABOUT YOUR ROLE 👀 As a Full Stack Engineer, you’ll work on our enterprise AI SaaS product https://joinpogo.ai/ and own meaningful parts of the product end-to-end.
title: Full Stack Engineer

confidence_reasons: 23 qualification lines need manual review; they were not fully assessed

unparsed.source: As a Full Stack Engineer, you'll work on our enterprise AI SaaS product https://joinpogo.ai/ and own meaningful parts of the product end-to-end. This is a hands-on role with real responsibility. Specifically, you will:
Build and own user-facing product features from idea to production
Work closely with engineering, product, and design to plan, architect, and ship features
You'll also partner with functional leaders across the organization (i.e., GTM, finance, customer support) to design and build internal tools to streamline operations and eliminate manual workflows.
You have strong product and design taste and a clear sense of what “good” looks like
You take ownership and are comfortable driving an entire part of a product
You manage your own time and priorities well
You're happy moving across frontend and backend when needed
You communicate clearly and work well with others, especially when things are ambiguous
You've built and maintained production systems used by real users
You're comfortable learning new tools and building things from scratch
Bonus:
Experience at early-stage startups or building your own products
Have heard of Animations.Dev http://Animations.Dev, Devouring Details https://devouringdetails.com/, or InterfaceCraft https://www.interfacecraft.dev/
WHY YOU MIGHT BE EXCITED ABOUT THIS OPPORTUNITY 🙌
Ship real products that get real usage, from customer-facing features to internal tools
Work cross-functionally. Partner with product, design, ops, GTM, data, and CS
Use the latest tech. Build with the latest coding tools and infrastructure
Move fast. Ship quickly and get rapid feedback from real users and teammates
WHY YOU MIGHT NOT BE EXCITED ABOUT US 👎

Priorities may shift quickly. Oftentimes, we're tackling very ambiguous problems that don't have clear-cut answers. While we make calculated bets, we have a strong culture of experimentation and we'll pivot as necessary based on what we're seeing in the data and what we're hearing from our users.

At times, you'll need to build things in a day: we live and breathe a value called “Calculated Speed”, which involves iterating and shipping weekly, rather than spending months going through complex processes or lengthy builds. Our engineers are some of the best in the world, which means anything you design today may be shipped next week.

We don't have structured management (yet!). We don't have the management overhead to provide direction every step of the way and we're looking for someone that gets energized by being able to run with things.

unparsed.source: We're looking for people who have already used AI to change how real work gets done.

You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You've built things that other people used, or that ran in production systems, and that measurably improved the speed or quality of their work.

You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new work becomes viable.

You learn the work quickly. You may have direct experience in sales development, sales operations, or marketing, or you quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of a new team. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next week.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment.
Minimum Requirements

Hands-on experience building and deploying AI-powered agents, tools, automations, or workflows that other people used or that ran as part of production systems, and that measurably improved the speed or quality of the work
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences
Comfort working across multiple workstreams and relationships simultaneously
Experience in a formal AI transformation or automation role where the job was substantially about identifying opportunities for workflow transformation and executing on them with hands-on builds
Experience in sales development, sales operations, revenue operations, marketing operations, or a closely adjacent function
In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

unparsed.source: We're looking for people who have already used AI to change how real work gets done.

You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You've built things that other people used, or that ran in production systems, and that measurably improved the speed or quality of their work.

You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new work becomes viable.

You learn the work quickly. You may have direct experience in sales development, sales operations, or marketing, or you quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of a new team. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next week.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment.

In-office expectations

unparsed.source: We're looking for people who have already used AI to change how real work gets done.

You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You've built things that other people used, or that ran in production systems, and that measurably improved the speed or quality of their work.

You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new work becomes viable.

You learn the work quickly. You may have direct experience in sales development, sales operations, or marketing, or you quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of a new team. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next week.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment.
Minimum Requirements

Hands-on experience building and deploying AI-powered agents, tools, automations, or workflows that other people used or that ran as part of production systems, and that measurably improved the speed or quality of the work
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences
Comfort working across multiple workstreams and relationships simultaneously
Experience in a formal AI transformation or automation role where the job was substantially about identifying opportunities for workflow transformation and executing on them with hands-on builds
Experience in sales development, sales operations, revenue operations, marketing operations, or a closely adjacent function
In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

items.source: Hybrid work at Stripe

unparsed.source: We're looking for people who have already lived the transformation they'll be driving for others. You've used AI to fundamentally change how work gets done, not as a novelty, but as your default operating mode.

You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You don't just know what AI can do in theory. You've built things that changed how real teams operate, and the people you built for actually use what you shipped. You build in real time alongside the people you support.

You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new programs become viable that weren't worth doing before. Then you build the thing, not just the slide.

You understand marketing work. You either have direct experience in marketing or quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of your assigned cohort. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, adapt your style to different people, and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next quarter.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment.
Minimum Requirements

Demonstrated, hands-on experience building and deploying AI-powered agents, tools, automations, or workflows that real people use in their actual work, whether that made existing processes meaningfully more efficient or made previously unviable work possible for the first time
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and adapt your style to different learners
Comfort working across multiple workstreams and relationships simultaneously (you'll be supporting 25–45 marketers at varying stages of their AI journey)
Track record of coaching, teaching, or enabling others, with evidence that people you've helped actually changed how they work
Experience in a formal AI transformation role where the job was substantially about identifying opportunities for workflow transformation and executing on them with hands-on builds
Experience helping people become more expert AI users and capable builders
In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You don't just know what AI can do in theory. You've built things that changed how real teams operate, and the people you built for actually use what you shipped. You build in real time alongside the people you support.

You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new programs become viable that weren't worth doing before. Then you build the thing, not just the slide.

You understand marketing work. You either have direct experience in marketing or quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of your assigned cohort. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, adapt your style to different people, and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next quarter.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment.
Minimum Requirements

Demonstrated, hands-on experience building and deploying AI-powered agents, tools, automations, or workflows that real people use in their actual work, whether that made existing processes meaningfully more efficient or made previously unviable work possible for the first time

Comfort working across multiple workstreams and relationships simultaneously (you'll be supporting 25–45 marketers at varying stages of their AI journey)
Track record of coaching, teaching, or enabling others, with evidence that people you've helped actually changed how they work

Experience helping people become more expert AI users and capable builders
In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

items.source: Hybrid work at Stripe

unparsed.source: We're looking for people who have already lived the transformation they'll be driving for others. You've used AI to fundamentally change how work gets done, not as a novelty, but as your default operating mode.

You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You don't just know what AI can do in theory. You've built things that changed how real teams operate, and the people you built for actually use what you shipped. You build in real time alongside the people you support.

You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new programs become viable that weren't worth doing before. Then you build the thing, not just the slide.

You understand marketing work. You either have direct experience in marketing or quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of your assigned cohort. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, adapt your style to different people, and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next quarter.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment.
Minimum Requirements

Demonstrated, hands-on experience building and deploying AI-powered agents, tools, automations, or workflows that real people use in their actual work, whether that made existing processes meaningfully more efficient or made previously unviable work possible for the first time
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and adapt your style to different learners
Comfort working across multiple workstreams and relationships simultaneously (you'll be supporting 25–45 marketers at varying stages of their AI journey)
Track record of coaching, teaching, or enabling others, with evidence that people you've helped actually changed how they work
Experience in a formal AI transformation role where the job was substantially about identifying opportunities for workflow transformation and executing on them with hands-on builds
Experience helping people become more expert AI users and capable builders
In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Eligibility for a Government background check and CAC issuance for access to DoD systems.

Military experience would be phenomenal, but it is not required. If you've served, especially in Army Aviation, you already understand the people we build for: how a unit runs, why readiness data has to be right, and what it costs when software gets in the way. That perspective makes you a better developer here from day one. If you haven't served, that's fine too. We'll teach you the mission, and a fresh set of eyes has its own value. Veterans, transitioning service members, Guard and Reserve members are strongly encouraged to apply.
DoD SkillBridge

Lulius is a DoD SkillBridge partner. If you're a service member in your final 180 days of service, you can apply to spend that time training and working with us through SkillBridge (the Career Skills Program for Soldiers), keeping your military pay and benefits while you build real experience on our products. With positions just outside Fort Rucker and in Reno/Tahoe, plus a remote option, many transitioning service members can do it close to where they already are. Talk to your command and transition office about eligibility, then reach out to us to set it up.
How we'll get to know you

In interviews, expect to walk us through something you built: how it works, where AI assisted, and what you had to fix when it got things wrong. We may ask you to extend it live with your own tools. We're looking for understanding and judgment, not memorized syntax.
Location and details

This is a full-time position based in Reno/Tahoe, Nevada, or in Daleville, Alabama, just outside Fort Rucker and close to the Army Aviation schoolhouses and units we build for. Remote is also an option for the right U.S.-based candidate. You'll work with our engineering team in Reno and Huntsville, with occasional travel to Fort Rucker, Redstone Arsenal, and supported units. Lulius Innovation is a veteran-owned small business headquartered in Reno/Tahoe, Nevada, building for Army Aviation and the broader military.
How to apply (bot check: please read)

To defeat bot and auto-generated applicants, we only review candidates who complete their application on our website. LinkedIn Easy Apply submissions without a matching application on our site will not be considered. Apply here, and include your resume, a link to your work, and a few lines on how you use AI in your work and what it has taught you:
https://www.luli.us/#/entry/junior-software-developer-agentic

Our engineers are some of the best in the world, which means anything you design today may be shipped next week.
